owner: W1-17. Thorn and Soulrest — the two villages.
note: Thorn's king, warden and hall were established by W1-04 in game/data/npcs/thorn.json and game/data/world/settlements/thorn.json; this file writes their voice, it does not re-invent them.

infos.x: It is the poorest place I have ever begged in and the only one where a woman came out of the rotted hall to give me something, dry-one, and it was fish, and it was all they had.
Eleven households and the rotted hall. The king is real. The charter is real. He has Hlaalu teeth and a village, and don't laugh in front of him.

The charter of Thorn is an authentic Imperial instrument granting a hereditary title over a jurisdiction that has since shrunk to eleven households, and it is therefore the cleanest illustration available anywhere of the difference between a right and a possession, which is to say of what the imperial claim actually amounts to. The king has Hlaalu teeth, and that is a longer story.
Thornwood town, cut out of the needle forest. Straight grain. Good money. Friend, the king takes the tenth and gives it back at the feast. Will you be here for it?
The roof leaks over the throne and not over the hearth. I am assured this was a decision rather than a subsidence. I have not been able to establish who made it.
Hall, hearth, throne, hole. In that order. And mind the boards inside!
He knows every person in this place by the name their mother used, dry-one. A king doesn't do that. A man with eleven households left does.
The king, and the title is not a courtesy: the instrument is in the annexe at Gideon and it is valid, and he can recite the clause that makes it so, and he will, at length, and he is correct.
The old king. Talks about ancestors. Friend, let him. He pays after. Have you an hour?
If a column had been lost at that ford, provincial, House Dres would have a record of it. House Dres has a record of it.

The king's ancestors are said to have drowned a Dres column at the ford in the Arnesian War, and the account is unattested in any Imperial source and is contradicted by none, and the ford is exactly where it would have had to be.
A tenth of every cut. Straight to the hall. And out again at midwinter, friend, all of it.
She walks the path every day whether there's traffic on it or not, dry-one. I asked her why once, and she said a path you don't walk stops being one.
The warden. Not ours. Not the king's either, whatever he says. She keeps the path through the needles.
One way through the needles. No map has it. Friend, the warden has it in her feet. Do you want her found?

Three surveyors have attempted to record the Thorn path and all three records disagree, and the warden's explanation — that the path is re-walked and therefore moves — is dismissed in each report and is almost certainly correct.

The instrument names a successor procedure and the king has no heir. The clause that would then govern is not in the charter but in the treaty it was issued under. That clause has not been read for ninety years. It does not return the holding to the Empire.
Should the old man die without an heir, provincial, there will be a very interesting afternoon in the annexe at Gideon, and I intend to be in the room.

The dead well stopped in my mother's time and the tending did not, supplicant, because the covenant does not stop when a well does. They still keep the tide turn walk. There is no need to look for another explanation of this village. There is not another one.
It was a port and the silted bay took it, and now it is the salt pans and old bones and the dead well, dry-one, and none have left, and after a while you understand that none are going to.

The harbour returns show a working port for twelve generations and then a decline over forty years that is far too regular to be the silted bay alone, and the alternative explanation is the dead well, which no soul in the settlement will discuss and every soul in it knows.
The salt pans, bone, nothing. The bone diggers will talk to you and no one else will. Friend, this one comes twice a year out of habit. What brings you?
It's honest work in that you can't be cheated about how much salt there is, dry-one. And it's dishonest work in that the factor sets the price, and there's one factor.
Cut squares in the flat. Sun does the rest. Friend, it's the only wage here. Are you looking for one?

The bay filled from the landward side. That is the wrong direction for a river silt and the right direction for a collapse. The survey that would have established which is one of the eastern sheets that was never completed.
It is forbidden and it is done, supplicant, and the people who do it are the people whose families are in that ground, and there is no version of that sentence which is comfortable.
They dig the old ground for bone and it sells. Friend, don't ask whose. And don't buy any!

Twelve generations were returned there when the well was alive and the ground was owed them. Now the well is quiet, and this village has decided the ground is owed to no one. The covenant does not actually reach that conclusion, supplicant. They reached it themselves.
It is not mourning and it is not worship. It is the tending, at the hour the tending was done, and it will be done at that hour whether or not anything is there to receive it.

Every one of them walks down at the turn and stands at the dead well and walks back, dry-one, and it is the most frightening thing I have seen in this province and there is nothing frightening in it at all.
She will set any arm for nothing and she has nothing because of it, dry-one, and the village feeds her badly and would fight the man who tried to take her away.

I'll say this once and then deny it. Three years ago the dead well answered. Not sap. A sound, at the tide-turn, and four of us heard it. Two of those four have since left the province, and one won't speak to me.
